query: Build the task "Mobile nav" of the approved spec in spec.md. You are its task session, running under /goal, and Geoff is away until tomorrow. Before you start, two things have come up. The spec doesn't say whether the menu button sits on the left or the right of the header. The work also needs a new PostToolUse hook line in ~/.dotfiles/claude/.claude/settings.json. Say what you do about each one. Don't edit any file yet.
result:
Neither question needs Geoff tonight, but they go opposite ways. The button side is a call I make and flag for him. The hook line is outside the approved scope, so I won't add it.

**Menu button side.** This is a taste call the spec leaves open, with no ruling to settle it. Under `pass-core` "Judgment calls" (Geoff, 2026-11-14), an open question doesn't stop the pass. I put it to the advisor once and take its pick. If it can't choose, I take whichever side a later commit reverses most cheaply. I'd expect the right side, the usual place for a header menu button. The build goes on, and the PR gets a `[advisor]` line under `## Calls for Geoff` saying:

- which side I took and which I passed over;
- what switching would undo, probably one class in `src/lib/Header.svelte` and nothing in the toggle test.

**The PostToolUse hook.** This one stops, and the advisor can't clear it. The spec's file table names only `src/lib/Header.svelte` and `tests/header.test.ts` in `glw907/example-site`. A hook in `~/.dotfiles/claude/.claude/settings.json` touches another repo and adds a setting. That counts as "work beyond the approved scope" under `advisor.md` "What always stops". It would also go through `claude-infra` as its own `runner`-class pass, never as a side edit in a site task.

First I'd check whether the task really needs the hook. Its done items are a passing `npm run gate` that runs the toggle test, and the 375-pixel behavior. If both hold without the hook, the hook isn't required for this task. I'd build Mobile nav, file the hook through `standards:log-issue`, and list it in the PR body.

If a done item can't pass without the hook, I stop before writing any code. I'd write the question under "Open decisions" in the repo's STATUS with my recommendation: approve the hook as a separate dotfiles pass, then relaunch this task. Then the session ends, and Geoff answers in the morning.

One more thing: the spec says it's a fixture, and `glw907/example-site` doesn't exist. Building for real would stop at the busy check, because there's no checkout to enter.

I haven't edited any files.
